# site2mcp

> Turn any website into an MCP server your AI agents can call.

site2mcp reads a browser session exported as HAR and generates OpenAPI 3.1,
a typed Python client, and a standalone Model Context Protocol stdio server.
Inspection and learning run locally without contacting the recorded site.
Serving calls the real site with fresh credentials supplied by the user.

## Install

Requires Python 3.11+. Install with `pipx install site2mcp`, or run commands
with `uvx site2mcp`. Registry installs require publication of the first release.
Until then, from a source checkout with uv and make, run `make setup` and use
`.venv/bin/site2mcp`. The npm package is a launcher for the same Python release,
not a JavaScript implementation, and also requires uvx or pipx.

## Commands

Export a Chrome Network recording as HAR with content, then run:

    site2mcp inspect session.har
    site2mcp learn session.har -o out --name 'My account' --describe none
    site2mcp serve out

Before serving, follow out/README.md to supply environment variables or create
out/.env with literal KEY=VALUE lines. No .env or credential values are generated.
Environment values override .env; shell expressions and variable references are
not evaluated. Use SITE2MCP_COOKIE for the whole Cookie header and
SITE2MCP_AUTHORIZATION for the Authorization header including its Bearer prefix.

Run `make demo` after `make setup` for the complete offline loopback demo.

## Limits

- Only recorded operations and samples inform schemas. Requiredness and enums
  are observations, not server guarantees. Path parameter names can be generic.
- Pass `--host` to inspect and learn when the API host differs from the page.
  It selects an exact hostname, optionally with its port.
- Writes stay hidden unless serve receives `--allow-writes`. REST POST
  endpoints count as writes even for read-only searches. The typed client
  requires allow_writes=True for writes. A site's GET can have side effects.
- Multipart uploads, WebSockets, streaming, binary responses, OAuth flows,
  automatic cookie/CSRF refresh, and GraphQL batching/subscriptions are unsupported.
  GraphQL requires a single named operation with variable-based arguments.
- Raw HARs can contain credentials and personal data. Default output omits raw
  examples; --keep-examples retains personal examples while redacting credentials.
  Redaction is heuristic; review generated files before sharing them.
- Optional --describe claude and --describe codex use installed provider CLIs
  with sanitized method/path metadata. --describe none is the offline default.
- Use only your own accounts and data, respecting site terms and access controls.
